A.note: Smoke plumes, the muzzle-flash glow and a flag show active battle, and the water has sparkle and texture. The buildings are still extruded blocks, and the smoke is a soft translucent blob. The ground is a bit noisy and flat. Of the four, this one best reads as a battle.

B.note: Calm, bright and clean, with no smoke or action, so the battle story is missing. The ships are tiny, and the ground is a speckled white noise texture. The orange-roofed block buildings look like game pieces, and the water is a flat gradient.

C.note: Same battle content as A. The ground is smoother and more muted, with less noisy streaking, so the town reads a little cleaner. It is slightly cleaner than A, but the buildings are still blocks and the smoke is vague.

D.note: Like B but with odd black building blocks that read as render glitches. There is no smoke or action, the ground is washed-out noise, and the ships are tiny.

why: C and A are the only versions that show an attack, with smoke, a muzzle flash and a flag, and C has the cleaner ground. B and D are static, washed-out and toy-like, and D adds odd black blocks.
top_fix_for_best: Replace the extruded block buildings and the soft smoke blobs with textured, varied roofs and walls, and with volumetric billowing smoke carrying visible cannon flashes and splashes. Add tiny troops and ship detail such as sails, hulls and broadside fire so the scale reads as a real battle.
